senses.gloss: עֵירֵר (v. עִרְעֵר I) [to stir up,] to protest, contest, object.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 1:2:3">Y. Gitt. I, 43ᶜ</cite> top <he>אם בא ועי׳ עררו בטל</he> if the husband comes and contests (the validity of his letter of divorce), his objection is null and void.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 1:2:3">Ib.</cite> <he>הוא ערר משנישאת הוא ע׳ וכ׳</he> it is all the same whether he objects after she has remarried or before it.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:1:2">Y. Keth. II, beg. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>נתאלמנה מי עוֹרֵר וכ׳</he> if she is a widow, who objects (opposes the woman’s claim)? <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 1:3">Gitt. I, 3</cite> <he>אם יש עליו עוֹרְרִים</he> if there are contestants against it (the letter of divorce); a. fr.

<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 2:2">Tosef. Sot. II, 2</cite> <he>אפי׳</he> … <he>המים מִתְעָרְרִין עליה</he> Var. (ed. Zuck. <he>המים היה מִתְרַעְרְעִין</he>, read: <he>המים מתר׳</he> or <he>מִתְעַרְעֲרִין</he>) even if she goes astray twenty years afterwards, the waters will be stirred up (work injury) in her body.
